system_note: What was billed: A41.9 (sepsis, unspecified) as principal diagnosis; R65.21 (septic shock), J13 (Streptococcus pneumoniae pneumonia), J96.01, J80, N17.9, J95.851 (VAP), B96.5 (Pseudomonas cause) and status Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis). What the record shows vs. governing policy and the resulting corrections: 1) Organism-specific sepsis coding - A41.9 (unspecified sepsis) is not supported because blood cultures identified Streptococcus pneumoniae on admission. Infectious Diseases documents: "Admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (now cleared)" (Infectious Diseases Consultation, p. 585). The sepsis policy explicitly maps Streptococcus pneumoniae to A40.3 (A40.3 is the organism-specific sepsis code) and states organism-specific codes should be used when an organism is identified: "Identified Organism: Streptococcus pneumoniae; ICD-10-CM Sepsis Code: A40.3; Additional Organism Code Needed?: No - organism embedded in code; CC/MCC Status: MCC" (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria › ICD-10-CM Organism-Specific Sepsis Code Selection Guide). Because an organism was identified on admission, A40.3 should be sequenced as the principal diagnosis with R65.21 reported as the severe sepsis / septic shock additional code per policy (R65.21 must be paired with an A40.-/A41.- code). The record also documents septic shock with elevated lactate and vasopressor initiation on admission: "met criteria for septic shock with a lactate of 5.1 mmol/L ... rapid-sequence intubation ... broad-spectrum antimicrobials and vasopressor support were initiated." (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 54). The ED note documents norepinephrine initiation: "For refractory hypotension with lactate 5.1 mmol/L, norepinephrine was started" (Emergency Department Provider Note, p. 54). Conclusion: A41.9 is miscoded given culture-confirmed S. pneumoniae sepsis - replace A41.9 with A40.3 (sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae) in principal position; retain R65.21. 2) Ventilator-associated pneumonia and organism-specific pneumonia coding - the chart documents a hospital-acquired VAP (day 6) with Pseudomonas identified and treated (Infectious Diseases: "Severe CAP complicated by day-6 VAP. Admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (now cleared); BAL pending." (Infectious Diseases Consultation, p. 585); Discharge/Transfer Summary: "resolved ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas)" (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 913)). Per the VAP policy, VAP must be POA=N and is supported when onset is >48 hours post-intubation and organism/culture and treatment are documented. The record meets that: provider documents VAP (day-6) and targeted therapy (cefepime) after bronchoscopy/BAL. Correct coding should include the VAP diagnosis (J95.851, POA=N) and the organism-specific pneumonia code for Pseudomonas (e.g., J15.1) rather than leaving only a generic B96.5; the VAP policy supports organism-specific pneumonia when cultures identify the pathogen and provider documents it. Action: keep J95.851 (POA=N) and replace B96.5 with the appropriate pneumonia code for Pseudomonas (J15.1) per documentation. 3) Resolved dialysis dependence - the discharge summary documents renal recovery and discontinuation of hemodialysis: "Renal function recovered and hemodialysis was discontinued;" (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 913). Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis) was billed POA=N on this claim but the record documents dialysis was discontinued before transfer/discharge; a dependence status code should not remain active after documented resolution. Action: remove Z99.2 from the final diagnosis list. 4) Status of ventilator dependence - discharge/transfer notes document a tracheostomy and ongoing ventilator/trach-collar weaning at transfer: "Tracheostomy on trach collar (FiO2 35%)." (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 913) and multiple RT/Consult notes document prolonged ventilation and >96 hours of ventilator support. Z99.11 (dependence on respirator[ventilator] status) is supported as active at transfer and should remain coded (POA=N is appropriate if dependence developed during the stay). 5) Other diagnoses/supporting items - J96.01 (acute hypoxemic respiratory failure), J80 (ARDS), N17.9 (AKI) and the listed complications (new AF, delirium, critical illness myopathy, IJ DVT, diabetes, COPD, HTN, hyperlipidemia) are all documented in the H&P, consults, progress notes and discharge summary and are supported (citations below). Where alternative specificity exists in the chart (e.g., problem list and consults show J44.1 for COPD acute exacerbation), use the most specific supported code. Corrective action applied (complete corrected diagnosis and procedure lists provided below). Key evidence and governing-policy citations are included in the evidence_cited section below to permit line-by-line auditability.
rationale_letter: Re: DRG audit determination - Claim MR_17 We completed a DRG-level documentation and coding audit of your inpatient stay (admit 07/01/2026 - transfer 11/21/2026). Our review compared the submitted claim line-level coding to the treating documentation and to the applicable coding policy guidance. Finding: Incorrect sepsis organism coding and an unsupported dialysis-dependence status code. Basis for finding: - The medical record documents positive admission blood cultures for Streptococcus pneumoniae. (Infectious Diseases Consultation, 07/06/2026: "Admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (now cleared); BAL pending.") Per the sepsis coding guidance, when an organism is identified the organism-specific sepsis code is required; Streptococcus pneumoniae maps to A40.3. (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria › ICD-10-CM Organism-Specific Sepsis Code Selection Guide: "Identified Organism: Streptococcus pneumoniae; ICD-10-CM Sepsis Code: A40.3 ..."). The chart also documents septic shock on presentation with elevated lactate and vasopressor initiation (History & Physical (Admitting), 07/01/2026: "met criteria for septic shock with a lactate of 5.1 mmol/L ... broad-spectrum antimicrobials and vasopressor support were initiated."; Emergency Department Provider Note, 07/01/2026: "For refractory hypotension with lactate 5.1 mmol/L, norepinephrine was started"). Under the policy, severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21) must be reported with the organism-specific sepsis code (A40.3). Therefore A41.9 (sepsis, unspecified organism) in principal position is not supported by the documented positive cultures and must be replaced with A40.3. - The record documents a hospital-acquired ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) on ICU day 6 with Pseudomonas identified and treated (Infectious Diseases and Discharge/Transfer Summary). Per the VAP guidance, J95.851 should be assigned with POA = N for confirmed VAP and organism-specific pneumonia coding (J15.1 for Pseudomonas) is indicated when cultures identify the pathogen. The submitted claim included B96.5 (Pseudomonas as cause) rather than the organism-specific pneumonia code; we corrected that to J15.1 and retained J95.851, POA=N. - The discharge summary documents renal recovery and discontinuation of hemodialysis prior to transfer: "Renal function recovered and hemodialysis was discontinued;" (Discharge / Transfer Summary, 11/21/2026). Because dialysis dependence resolved prior to discharge/transfer, the status code Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis) is not supported and should be removed from the final diagnosis list. Correction applied: The claim's corrected, complete diagnosis list and procedure list are provided below. This correction changes the principal diagnosis sequencing (position 1) from A41.9 to A40.3 and removes Z99.2; it also replaces B96.5 with J15.1 to reflect organism-specific VAP documentation. R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) remains as an additional code in support of the septic shock documentation. J95.851 (VAP) remains as POA=N and is supported by the ID documentation and BAL/culture-directed therapy. All billed procedures were supported in the record and remain unchanged. Corrected (final) diagnosis list (position 1 = principal): 1. A40.3 - Sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae (principal) 2. R65.21 - Severe sepsis with septic shock 3. J96.01 - Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia 4. J80 - Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) 5. J13 - Pneumonia due to Streptococcus pneumoniae 6. N17.9 - Acute kidney failure, unspecified 7. J95.851 - Ventilator associated pneumonia (POA = N) 8. J15.1 - Pseudomonas pneumonia (VAP) 9. I48.91 - Unspecified atrial fibrillation 10. F05 - Delirium due to known physiological condition 11. G72.81 - Critical illness myopathy 12. I82.C11 - Acute embolism and thrombosis of right internal jugular vein 13. E11.65 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia 14. J44.1 - COPD with (acute) exacerbation (use most specific supported code) 15. I10 - Essential (primary) hypertension 16. E78.5 - Hyperlipidemia, unspecified 17. Z99.11 - Dependence on respirator [ventilator] status Corrected procedure list (complete; unchanged except as noted): - 0BH17EZ - Insertion of endotracheal airway into trachea, via natural or artificial opening - 02HV33Z - Insertion of infusion device into superior vena cava, percutaneous approach - 03HY32Z - Insertion of monitoring device into upper artery, percutaneous approach - 05H93JZ - Insertion of infusion device into right femoral vein, percutaneous approach - 0BJ08ZZ - Inspection of tracheobronchial tree, via natural or artificial opening endoscopic - 0B110F4 - Bypass trachea to cutaneous with tracheostomy device, open approach - 0DH60UZ - Insertion of feeding device into stomach, percutaneous endoscopic approach - 5A1D90Z - Assistance with respiratory ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours - 5A1D80Z - Performance of urinary filtration, prolonged intermittent, less than 6 hours per day If you disagree with these corrections, please provide provider-authored documentation (attestation or clarified discharge/problem statement) that contradicts the charted culture results or documents ongoing dialysis dependence at discharge. Absent such documentation, the above corrected code set reflects the chart and applicable coding policy.

evidence_cited.excerpt: Severe CAP complicated by day-6 VAP. Admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (now cleared); BAL pending.

In the ED the patient met criteria for septic shock with a lactate of 5.1 mmol/L that failed to clear after a 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid bolus. Given profound hypoxemic respiratory failure and depressed mental status the patient underwent rapid-sequence intubation, and broad-spectrum antimicrobials and vasopressor support were initiated.
